clue.text: Safe vessel, one showing no sign of age

definitions.text: one showing no sign of age

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe, as in a safe-cracker or peterman
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: A secure container is described, along with someone who never seems to get any older.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER as a safe is old underworld slang. The definition points to J. M. Barrie's boy who never grows up.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrie's hero is the boy who refuses to grow up, so the name is used of anyone who stays youthful.

clue.text: We are its ruin, so to speak

indicators.note: ruin works as a verb here: the letters of the preceding words are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone laments that we are the cause of something's downfall, adding a casual 'so to speak'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruin' reads as a noun belonging to 'its', but it is the anagram signal on WE ARE ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are verbal hedges used to show an expression is not meant literally.

clue.text: Beg for a free show to follow in French

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the first, following it

parts.note: en is the French word for in
a treat is an entertainment given free to someone

explanation.surface: Someone asks for complimentary entertainment to come next, in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' puts the free show after the French word, so the French piece comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg and to entreat both mean to ask earnestly and humbly for something.

clue.text: Timber and mineral found on land

parts.note: ash is a common hardwood timber
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: Wood and minerals have been discovered on dry ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore describes being on the shore or on dry ground rather than at sea.

clue.text: The Greeks had a word for it. I've discovered

definitions.text: The Greeks had a word for it
definitions.meaning: the Greek exclamation famously cried by Archimedes in his bath
the literal meaning of that Greek exclamation is 'I have found it'

explanation.surface: A remark that Greek has a term for something, followed by a cry of discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition plays on the saying 'the Greeks had a word for it'; here the word itself is Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes' cry on solving the problem of displacement translates as 'I have found it'.

clue.text: Try to look smart in order to go courting?

definitions.meaning: ironing a jacket and trousers is an effort to appear well turned out
to pursue a romantic suit is to woo someone, often with a proposal of marriage

explanation.surface: A suitor smartens up before going out to woo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' carries two senses: a set of clothes to be ironed, and an old word for wooing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing clothes makes one look tidy, while pressing a romantic suit means urging one's courtship.

clue.text: Used influence to get a job as a puppeteer?

definitions.text: Used influence to get a job
definitions.meaning: employed connections behind the scenes to secure a position
a marionette operator literally tugs on cords to move the figures

explanation.surface: Someone secured employment through contacts, much as a marionette operator works.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for secret influence is read literally as what a puppeteer does with a marionette.
explanation.definitionFit: Using hidden influence is likened to tugging the cords of a marionette, which a puppeteer does literally.

clue.text: Test match

parts.note: not the cricket fixture between nations but a trial run of a match in the wedding sense

explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket game; here 'test' means trial and 'match' a union of two people.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples living together before committing are trying out a union, a matrimonial experiment.

clue.text: Keep watch on this

parts.note: not guarding something but keeping a pocket watch secured by a chain

explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep watch' suggests sentry duty; it means holding a pocket watch on its chain, a style named after Prince Albert.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name for a watch chain fastened across a waistcoat, after Queen Victoria's consort.

clue.text: Greek island-one with a colony in Africa at one time

definitions.text: colony in Africa at one time

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A Greek island and a former African colony are linked.
explanation.definitionFit: This British colony in southern Africa became modern Zimbabwe and Zambia.

clue.text: A small Scotch

parts.note: not a modest measure of whisky but the Scots word meaning little

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' suggests whisky; it means Scottish, so this is the Scottish word for small.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish speech the everyday word for little is this one.

clue.text: Part of a head place of worship

definitions.meaning: the flat region on either side of the forehead
a building dedicated to a god, such as a Hindu or ancient Greek shrine

explanation.surface: A part of the skull and a holy building are set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the side of the forehead and a building for religious worship.

clue.text: Wiling to back scholar and provide means

indicators.note: to back means to go backwards, so the scholar's abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar
to enable is to provide the means for something

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to support an academic and fund them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' looks like supporting the scholar, but it means going backwards, turning his degree abbreviation round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is compliant and agreeable, ready to go along with things.

clue.text: A female devoted to order

parts.note: not a tidy woman but one devoted to a religious order

explanation.walkthrough: 'order' suggests tidiness; it is a religious order of sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who has taken vows within a religious community is a sister of that order.

clue.text: Apart and sure to play around

indicators.note: the letters fool about and regroup into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone separated is sure to be unfaithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play around' suggests infidelity; it is the anagram signal on AND SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn asunder means pulled into pieces, separated.

clue.text: Note in sound currency

indicators.note: sound as in heard: the word for currency is said aloud

parts.note: dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: A banknote in stable money is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound currency' reads as stable money; 'sound' means heard. DOH is the first note of the tonic sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: In sol-fa singing, the first syllable of the scale names a musical tone.

clue.text: Spaniards accepting article for their wives

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: senor is the Spanish title for a man
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Spanish men take in a piece of writing for the sake of their wives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their wives' is plural like the answer: Spanish married women.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish men's wives are addressed by the Spanish title for married women.

clue.text: Musicians get together to make it up

definitions.text: Musicians get together to make it up

parts.words: Musicians get together to make it up
parts.note: not a reconciliation but players combining to form a group

explanation.walkthrough: 'make it up' suggests settling a quarrel; it means to constitute a group of performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of players performing together forms a small orchestra or band.

clue.text: Nuance obvious to an individual

parts.note: overt means open and obvious
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: Subtle shading is obvious to one particular person.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertone or subtle implied quality is a shade of meaning, a nuance.

clue.text: They tell us how to write endless bad verse, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters might be put together some other way
the final letter of the word verse is cut off

explanation.surface: A teacher's guides explain how to write poor poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final E of VERSE; 'perhaps' then rearranges BAD with VERS.
explanation.definitionFit: These parts of speech modify verbs, describing manner, such as quickly or slowly.

clue.text: Title used in all-in wrestling?

parts.note: a wrestling grip with no restrictions, read as the legal title to land

explanation.walkthrough: 'Title' suggests a championship belt; it is a legal title to property, punned on an unrestricted wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright legal ownership of land and buildings, held indefinitely, is this kind of tenure.

clue.text: Threaten to get money

parts.note: a description of obtaining cash by intimidation

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the crime of blackmail-style demands.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain cash or concessions by force or threats is this crime.

clue.text: Vegetables that need to be set in soon

indicators.note: set as in arranged: the letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener's bulbs need to be planted shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' suggests planting, apt since these are grown from sets; it is the anagram signal on IN SOON.
explanation.definitionFit: These pungent bulbs are kitchen vegetables.

clue.text: Make a mistake and throw out the drink

indicators.note: out here means outside, so the throw goes round the mistake

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A clumsy waiter slips and hurls the beverage away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throw out' reads as discarding the drink; 'out' really means outside, so the throw wraps round the mistake. A coconut shy is a fairground stall where balls are thrown at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: This fortified wine from Jerez is a classic aperitif.

clue.text: Contend it's a quarter past six

indicators.note: past means after, so the quarter comes after the six

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
east is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone claims the time is quarter past six.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' is a compass point, here E for east.
explanation.definitionFit: To compete or strive with rivals is to contend.

clue.text: I react in disaster instantly

indicators.note: the letters come to grief and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes their immediate response to a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' is the anagram signal; 'in' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in a moment, immediately.

clue.text: Common sort of friend Dickens wrote about

definitions.meaning: shared by two or more people

definitions.text: sort of friend Dickens wrote about
definitions.meaning: Our ___ Friend is Dickens's last completed novel

explanation.surface: A reference to an ordinary kind of friend in a Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Shared interests are common to both parties, and Dickens's last completed novel is titled 'Our ___ Friend'.

clue.text: It enables weighty measures to be taken-at the end of the fiscal year?

definitions.text: It enables weighty measures to be taken-at the end of the fiscal year?

parts.words: It enables weighty measures to be taken-at the end of the fiscal year?
parts.note: a weighing device using a coil, punned on the season when the British tax year ends and accounts are settled

explanation.walkthrough: The UK fiscal year ends in early April, so its closing account falls in the season after winter; the phrase is also a coiled weighing device.
explanation.definitionFit: A coiled scale measures weight by stretching, and a tax year closing in April gives a seasonal statement of accounts.
